note: Geometry and paper presets. pageW/pageH and all margins are in points. "faces" is the card's natural count -- a double-sided sheet is two faces -- and is the anchor auto starts from, not a hard limit. "screen" marks a preset that is never printed, so it has no back to duplex and its faces need not come in pairs. The screen presets are grouped by the *shape* of the glass, because a wallpaper fits or does not fit on shape alone, and split by size where one shape spans sizes far enough apart to matter to the type: each is sized from the smallest diagonal in its band, so the card is scaled up on a bigger screen and never down, and a point on the card is a point on the glass or a shade more -- which is what the per-script legibility floors, also in points, are stated against. "models" is the roll of phones a screen preset covers, shown as text under the ladder that chooses it, because the shape a preset is named for does not tell a reader whether their phone is in it.

card-7x5-4col.name: 7×5in landscape · 4 columns
card-7x5-4col.note: Matches the reference sheet: 1.662in columns, 0.0507in gap.

phone-1col.name: Phone screen · 1 column
phone-1col.note: 2.5x5.5in, which is the physical size of a 6in phone screen -- so the type sizes and the per-script legibility floors, all in points, are what the reader actually sees. Whole pixels at every dpi the panel offers: 375x825, 750x1650, 1500x3300. One column, because two would be 79pt wide against the 115-138pt every other preset gives a column.
phone-1col.models: Any phone: a plain 2.5x5.5in card near 2.2:1, cut to no screen in particular. The other presets here are cut to a named shape and a named size.

phone-19-5x9.name: iPhone 12-17 · Galaxy S22-S26 · 6.1in, 2.17:1
phone-19-5x9.note: The commonest phone shape, 19.5:9, at the standard sizes. The logical aspects in the group run 2.164 (iPhone 12/13/14, 390x844pt) through 2.167 (Galaxy S22-S26, 1080x2340) and 2.168 (iPhone 14 Pro/15/16, 393x852pt) to 2.174 (iPhone 16 Pro/17, 402x874pt) -- half a percent end to end, which is a pixel and a half of crop on a 6in screen, so one preset covers all of them. Sized from 6.1in, the smallest standard iPhone; a 6.3in iPhone 17 or a 6.2in Galaxy S25 scales it up 3%. Apple point resolutions from the per-model tech specs at support.apple.com (121029 for the 16, 125089 for the 17, and siblings), cross-checked against ios-resolution.com; Samsung native resolutions from the model pages at gsmarena.com. Pixel 4a (5.81in) and Pixel 5 (6.0in) are this shape too and scale it down 5% and 2%.
phone-19-5x9.models: The 6.1-6.3in sizes, 19.5:9: iPhone 12, 13, 14, 15, 16 and 17, each in its standard and Pro form, and the 16e and 17e · Galaxy S22, S23, S24, S25 and S26 · Pixel 4a and Pixel 5. A Plus, Max, Air or Galaxy Ultra is the same shape on bigger glass -- it fits this card, but the iPhone Plus & Max preset is cut for it.

phone-19-5x9-max.name: iPhone Plus & Max · Galaxy Ultra · 6.5in, 2.17:1
phone-19-5x9-max.note: The same 19.5:9 shape as the standard iPhones and the Galaxy S, sized for the big ones: 6.5in (iPhone Air, 420x912pt) through 6.9in (iPhone 17 Pro Max, 440x956pt; Galaxy S25/S26 Ultra, 1440x3120). A separate preset because the shape does not fix the size: a 6.7in Plus is a tenth more glass than a 6.1in iPhone, and a card sized from 6.1in comes out a tenth larger than it needs to be on it, so a tenth fewer rows fit than the screen could hold. Sized from 6.5in, the smallest in the band, so nothing here is scaled down; the two 6.4in Galaxy FE models are the exception, at 2% under. Sources as for the 6.1in preset.
phone-19-5x9-max.models: The 6.5-6.9in sizes, 19.5:9: iPhone 14, 15 and 16 Plus · iPhone 12 through 17 Pro Max · iPhone Air · Galaxy S22+ through S26+ · Galaxy S24, S25 and S26 Ultra · Galaxy S21/S23/S24/S25/S26 FE · Galaxy S25 Edge · Pixel 6 Pro and Pixel 7 Pro.

phone-19-5x9-mini.name: iPhone mini · 5.4in, 2.17:1
phone-19-5x9-mini.note: 19.5:9 again (375x812pt, 2.1653), sized from the 5.4in diagonal of the iPhone 12 mini and 13 mini. Its own preset because the 6.1in card scales *down* 11% here, and a type size 11% under the floor it was chosen against is a phrase the reader cannot read. Point resolution from support.apple.com/111877 (12 mini) and /111873 (13 mini).
phone-19-5x9-mini.models: iPhone 12 mini and iPhone 13 mini, 5.4in. The same 19.5:9 shape as every other iPhone since the 12, sized for the smallest glass Apple made it in.

phone-20x9.name: Pixel · most Android · 6.2in, 2.22:1
phone-20x9.note: 20:9, the Pixel shape and much of Android. Not quite one number: the base Pixels since the 9 are 2424x1080 (2.244) and the Pro tier is 2856x1280 (2.231) or 2992x1344 (2.226), which Google's own spec sheets round to 20:9 or call 20.08:9 -- a 1% spread, against the 2.4% step down to 19.5:9. Sized from a 6.2in diagonal; a 6.7in Pixel Pro XL scales it up 8%, a 6.1in Pixel 8a down 2%. Native resolutions from the Pixel and Galaxy model pages at gsmarena.com and the Pixel articles at en.wikipedia.org, which carry Google's published figures.
phone-20x9.models: 20:9, from 6.1in to 6.9in: every Pixel from the 5a to the 11 Pro XL except the 6 Pro and 7 Pro, which are 19.5:9 · Galaxy S20, S20+, S20 Ultra, S20 FE, S21, S21+ and S21 Ultra, before Samsung moved the line to 19.5:9 · much of the rest of Android.

phone-19-3x9.name: Galaxy S22/S23 Ultra · 6.8in, 2.14:1
phone-19-3x9.note: 19.3:9 (1440x3088, 2.1444), which Samsung used for exactly two phones: the Galaxy S22 Ultra and S23 Ultra, both 6.8in. The S24 Ultra moved the panel to 1440x3120 -- exactly 19.5:9 -- and the S25 and S26 Ultra stayed there, so "Galaxy S Ultra" is no longer one shape and this preset names the two it is. Sized from 6.8in. Native resolutions from the model pages at gsmarena.com.
phone-19-3x9.models: Galaxy S22 Ultra and Galaxy S23 Ultra, 6.8in -- the only two Samsung phones at 19.3:9. An S24, S25 or S26 Ultra is 19.5:9 and belongs with the iPhone Plus & Max preset.

phone-16x9.name: iPhone SE · older Android · 4.7in, 1.78:1
phone-16x9.note: 16:9 (375x667pt, 1.7787), as on the iPhone SE and Android before the tall screens. Sized from the SE's 4.7in diagonal. The short screen is why the clock band is still near a third of it: the lock screen's furniture is anchored to the top and roughly fixed in size, so it takes a similar fraction of a 667pt screen as of an 852pt one. Point resolution from support.apple.com/111882 (SE 2nd generation) and /111866 (SE 3rd).
phone-16x9.models: iPhone SE, 2nd generation (2020) and 3rd generation (2022), 4.7in -- and the iPhone 6, 6s, 7 and 8, which are the same 375x667pt screen · Android before the tall screens.

phone-18x9.name: Older Android · 5.8in, 2.00:1
phone-18x9.note: 18:9, the first generation of tall Android screens, 2017-2018. Sized from a 5.8in diagonal. No model roll: the sourcing pass behind the other presets covered the Galaxy S line from the S20 and the Pixel line from the 4a, and this shape is older than both, so it names a ratio rather than phones it has not checked.
phone-18x9.models: The tall Android screens of 2017 and 2018, at a flat 18:9 (2.00) -- the step between the old 16:9 and today's 19.5:9 and 20:9. A phone of that generation is the one case here with no model roll behind it.

tablet-3x2.name: iPad · tablet · 10.9in, 1.44:1
tablet-3x2.note: A tablet in portrait, near 3:2 (820x1180pt, 1.4390). Wide enough for two columns. Sized from a 10.9in diagonal. No clock band by default, unlike the phone presets: an iPad's lock screen puts the clock at the top too, but nothing published says how much of a tablet it covers, and a guess at a third of a 644pt page is a third of the card. Point resolutions from support.apple.com/111840 (iPad 10th generation) and /122241 (iPad Air 11in).
tablet-3x2.models: iPad 10.9in (10th generation), iPad 11in (11th generation) and iPad Air 11in -- all 820x1180pt, 1.44:1. An iPad Pro 11in is 834x1210pt (1.45:1) and the 13in iPads are 1.33:1: close, but not this shape.
